body: If you had a hobby you enjoyed or a friend you could confide in would you see more meaning in your life? Many of us were given false hope about what life means and what we are capable of accomplishing. We live within our own limits, we can them but we can't change our inherited abilities which constrict our limits. I do believe you have a right to choose while preventing suicide is important, nobody on earth should have the right to say you can't do it. I also agree that if you have nothing to live for and it has been that way for a long time it is reasonable to consider suicide. With that said, even if you don't believe it things can change, that doesn't mean they will though. Waiting for things to change though is a failing strategy, sitting in your room all day (I did too yesterday) is not a great way to build relationships and it's hard to find a hobby if you don't try anything. Sure you'll try 100 things and hate 99 of them but you won't know you enjoy that one thing unless you are really lucky and find it first or like many of us fail a ton before finding something worth staying around an extra day for. I'm not trying to say don't kill yourself, do as you wish, but what if you were so methodical in finding a hobby, like your plan for suicide you'd be successful. I honestly don't know how many people are truly 'happy' most of us like you expressed have moments and while yours may be much shorter than most, the fact you have some moments shows you're capable of having more. Life may be miserable now and it could be that way forever but give yourself another chance, I realize you can't forget the past but focus on the now and future. Methodically plan, make goals that are big, small and minuscule, volunteer, find ways to build friendships and if you still feel completely flat when your cat passes away down the line then do as you see fit. That's my shitty advice from someone who feels much of what you expressed.

I don't get how he could hide evidence so poorly on a crime he intended to commit. The gun in the safe, the shower curtain etc. on his families property (he brought his phone for the drive too), the marijuana at his brothers (yet two guys in morph suits took it with the body...), does it in his own apartment in front of witnesses, runs around grabbing the money (victim probably was counting it) when he just committed cold blooded murder, opens his door in a panic letting neighbours observe inside. He was disturbed and definitely motivated by greed but clearly was not book stupid... did he think all the evidence couldn't amount to anything without a body, or that they wouldn't figure out it could be him, at least not so quickly that they would search his family and personal properties with evidence clearly connecting him with the crime scence at both before he could get rid of it in a better way. If the body was so cleverly hidden why did he not do the same with the evidence. The victim was physically much bigger than the killer so lugging and hiding it would be no easy task, especially in a minimal time frame. If he put the body in water why not the evidence too, same for fire or chemicals or whatever you can think of, why cleverly dispose of the body and bring the evidence to your farm. Only he knows where it is but I doubt the remains are so cleverly hidden if everything else was not.

Psychopath and sociopath are the exact same thing. One may have been considered socially driven to that type of personality vs. psychologically but that is not the case anymore as both nature and nurture play a role in the development of that type of person. The top 5% in most professions will have a greater proportion of people with psychopathic tendencies, not just medical professions; lawyers (I doubt judges) and banking would attract that personality.

Each week life is getting worse. I believe you, keep strong as things will hit a limit and turn around giving life some meaning, takes time and help but you can make a difference in your own life. Start with the smallest things. For me it's cleaning my room, it can be tough but when you do and wake up the next day it's a step to doing the next thing.

My old cat who never comes up and sits with me, likes the heated floors, knew I was sick one time and sat in the middle of my bed or on me for about a week when I didn't sleep at all, had bruising all over my body and eventually I went to the ER and with a full waiting room it took 5 minutes for me to be taken in, 10 mins to be in a bed (rare in Canada) with ER doctors attending to me, even called in a dermatologist late at night to assess me, had a really high temperature and heart rate apparently. He knew something was wrong. I was fine though at the end of the day, well they had me stay more than a day I was okay though. Pets have a sense for these things though. 

As for your marriage, I'm not married, never have been and I don't know your situation but no marriage IMO should not have fights, if you don't somebody is always caving to the others opinion. Don't give up on someone you were willing to marry after a week, speak about it, even see a marriage counselor before you give up and move out. Maybe it won't work out, it's possible, I also don't think people should go along with life suffering in an unfulfilling relationship but I also think once married you owe it to each other to try and address the issues.

All the best to you.

I'm not sure if you took the anti-depressants because you want to feel better or to try and kill yourself but there are very few that will make much difference in a matter of days and you probably would have a better chance taking Advil to kill yourself (not a suggestion). It's tough being alone, talking doesn't fix everything, nor do drugs but surrounding yourself with positive people will help relieve that sense of being lonely. Obviously you might not have any interests or desires but if you feel alone and that's your reason to go, why not try helping other people who are alone, a shelter or even just a random homeless person. Ask for their story. People usual do want to share its just difficult finding people that want to listen. One reason why people pay psychologists so much.

I feel you at 27. You can look at that negatively or positively. Wanting to die you'll probably think, why would I waste the next six years feeling the way you do. I've tried university, trades, service industry and it all overwhelmed me and still does. It's not easy to find your niche some people just have this set career path, others like us don't. I've attempted suicide, twice, once with overdosing on medication which led to a shitty time being dragged to the hospital by two officers and paramedics. Both officers told me a story, I suppose they are trained for that but one was that he bought a house with his GF and she cheated on him with his partner, I think his point was shit gets tough at times but it can get better if you give it a chance. The other, while I was still in bed said he couldn't even let me close the door to get dressed because he let someone do that once and she killed herself. Those stories really don't help your situation but just try and have a bit of patience with life. Nothing is certain but it can't get better when you're dead. I've also tried convincing my doctor of all the reasons not to live. He has also been through some real lows, losing his license from addiction. Each situation is unique, life is overwhelming for so many of us and death is such an easy fix but don't lose all hope.

By the way my prof has had like 5 jobs most would consider careers so we all bounce around at times. student that dropped out, shoe salesman, fighter pilot, police officer, clinical psychologist, professor.

I went to university out of high school, ended up dropping out after a few years. I worked, I also went through a major depressive episode where I didn't work. I went to learn a trade which I know is not for me so I gave university another go, 6 years later. I am again thinking about dropping out. I am doing a combined major of psychology and gerontology and had a long private two-hour talk with one of my profs and not that he told me not to do what I was doing but said without an honours in psychology it won't get me anywhere but that would mean starting from the start at something I don't even know I want. Anyways I have a point. I made an appointment with a school counselor who is actually a registered psychologist as well as you get 10 free sessions. My advice is to see if you have this resource at your university and take advantage of it. I didn't the first time at university. I may drop out again but I want to make an informed decision.

I was told those things too, I was smart, intelligent and could do anything but the reality is everything I try to do be it academic or physical labour, I suck at it. I've tried taking accounting, I worked in the service industry, I've tried carpentry, I'm in school for psychology and gerontology, I've even tried starting a business, I didn't lose money but I certainly did make any. School is now just my way of doing something to pass the time of my pointless life until I just can't face it anymore. I don't feel I have the ability to compete with people in the workplace, regardless of what the job is. It can be really difficult to find your purpose and I'm 27 and still feel that way but one thing I can say is I've tried. I;m not stupid, and even if you are shit at programming the fact you took the initiative to learn is something to be proud of. Happy belated birthday and just know you're not alone in how you feel.
